title: The FreeMPE Project
text:
Preface
This is a Quarto book.
To learn more about Quarto books visit https://quarto.org/docs/books.

title: 1  Introduction
text:
After spending some time going back and forth with ChatGPT about how I like to play music, what I like about the Roli ecosystem, and how their current business affairs are panning out, I decided that I wanted to do what I can to keep this new, awesome technology alive and accessible regardless of what may or may not happen to Roli.
I’m going to take a brief moment to philosophise on the state of things, if you don’t mind.
I think most would agree that we would pay people for good things in 2026 if

we support its intended use and promised impact on us and the world at large,
we can afford the thing,
it’s worth it holistically and presently, given the time in their life and circumstances they perceive to come from their decision to buy it.

What’s clear is that in late-stage capitalism, one or more of these premises is being violated. When a software pirate violates it, most people believe they are violating principle 2. But pirates can have that, and components of 1 and 3 involved in their decision.
I hope that readers can understand that this project does not use principle 2 as a singular reason for its existence, but does acknowledge that the rising cost of living crisis in the western world is not being helped by increasing costs, encroaching subscriptions, and general enshittification of things we’re supposed to do to get away from stress. Things like music.
This is not a dig on Roli, music business, music technologists, or anyone involved in the production of the Seaboard/Lightpad, Noise/Equator etc. I love and respect these products and their creators. But I just believe, deeply and fundamentally, that knowledge belongs to everyone. To see the phenomenon of MPE disappear with the company Roli, would be like if the we lived in a different timeline where the guy who was going to sign the papers to start selling Akai MPCs decided not to go to work that day, and as a result we all live without samplers.
I do not want to live in that world, and today, AI exists as a reasoning engine that can help us put many, many, many millions of sentences together, summarize them, and spit them back out ot us with a plan.
Well, this project is the culmination of many many conversations with my own ChatGPT instance, but also with several individuals on the internet and comment sections. My philosophy is laid bare in this file, which you are welcome to examine and is tracked by Git — there is no AI intervention in this file. It is what I truly believe should come of this project.
Everyone should be able to see MPE the same way I saw an electric guitar pedal for the first time, or the first time I used VirtualDJ on my beat up old laptop for the first time, or your first drum machine — whatever it may be, we can’t afford to let the technological know-how cannot disappear just because someone enterprising put it behind a paywall.
Let’s free MPE, y’all.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
2.1 Mission
FreeMPE is a preservation and interoperability project for expressive electronic musical instruments.
Its purpose is to help musicians retain practical ownership of hardware they have legitimately purchased when essential functionality depends on proprietary configuration software, licensing infrastructure, cloud services, abandoned applications, or vendors that can no longer support their products.
The initial case study is ROLI hardware, especially:
The project should eventually be useful to other MPE and expressive-MIDI devices.
The long-term aspiration is:
FreeMPE should become both:

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
2 × Seaboard Blocks
1 × Lightpad Block
1 × LUMI Block




A musician should be able to buy an expressive controller, keep it for decades, and continue configuring and performing with it even if its manufacturer disappears.



standalone open-source tooling where missing tooling must be recreated; and
a landing space for compatible open-source work that already exists elsewhere.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.1 Layer 0 — Standards
Document the standard behavior underneath everything:

MIDI
MIDI 2.0 where relevant
MPE
USB MIDI
Bluetooth MIDI
SysEx
HID or vendor-specific USB interfaces where discovered

Do not reverse-engineer a proprietary mechanism if the desired behavior is already exposed through a standard interface.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.2 Layer 1 — Observation
Tools for answering:

What is this device actually sending and receiving?

Produce reproducible captures of:

USB descriptors
MIDI messages
MPE channel behavior
SysEx traffic
BLE services where relevant
configuration changes
startup/shutdown behavior

Prefer passive capture before active probing.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.3 Layer 2 — Protocol documentation
Translate observations into human-readable specifications.
Example conceptual record:
set_pitch_bend_range(value)
rather than merely:
F0 00 ... F7
Every discovered message should document:

direction
trigger
payload
expected response
device/model
firmware tested
persistence
confidence

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.4 Layer 3 — Open control library
Implement the protocol independently.
Conceptually:
freempe
    devices/
        seaboard_block
        lightpad_block
        lumi_block
    midi/
    mpe/
    transport/
    protocols/
The library should not require a GUI.
Everything important should eventually be callable programmatically.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.5 Layer 4 — CLI
Example future interface:
freempe list

freempe inspect "Seaboard Block"

freempe mpe on

freempe bend-range 48

freempe sensitivity pressure 0.72

freempe lightpad layout chromatic

freempe backup device-backup.json

freempe restore device-backup.json
Syntax is illustrative until the protocol is understood.
The CLI becomes the reference implementation because it is:

inspectable;
scriptable;
testable;
portable;
easy to preserve.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
8.6 Layer 5 — GUI
Only after the protocol/library is stable, provide an approachable open replacement for vendor configuration tools.
The GUI should call the same library as the CLI.
Do not bury device knowledge exclusively inside GUI code.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.1 M0 — Freeze the lifeboats
Archive legitimate documentation, installers, firmware and version information while available.
No reverse engineering required.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.2 M1 — Offline survival matrix
For all four current ROLI devices, establish exactly what works with:
Internet disconnected.
Produce the compatibility matrix.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.3 M2 — MPE independence
Demonstrate each suitable controller driving at least one non-ROLI MPE instrument without proprietary synthesis software.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.4 M3 — Configuration dependency map
Identify every setting that presently requires Dashboard or another ROLI application.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.5 M4 — First open configuration
Choose one harmless configuration parameter.
Observe official behavior.
Reproduce it independently.
Document it.
This is the first true FreeMPE milestone.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.6 M5 — Read-only inspector
Create:
freempe inspect
that can identify supported connected devices and report everything safely observable.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.7 M6 — Minimal open dashboard
Configure the handful of parameters necessary for ordinary MPE performance without ROLI software.

title: 2  FreeMPE
text:
18.8 M7 — Preservation community
Publish protocol documentation, compatibility information, contribution procedures and carefully licensed OSS tooling.
Then expand beyond ROLI.

title: 3  Human intent routing
text:
3.1 When an experiment may run
Every meaningful turn begins with a human intention: what the person wants to understand, change, make, or preserve. Software is one possible response; it is not the default container for the intention.
Create the intention specification with $speckit-specify. The project-local Spec Kit template records the goal, uncertainty, constraints, completion rule, and route. Select the smallest route that can complete the intention.
An experiment is not authorized by curiosity alone, nor by a Manual page. Its intention specification must select preservation investigation and state:
The corresponding Manual page then supplies the visible procedure, local artifacts, and check. If the outcome suggests software, begin a new software-development intention rather than silently extending the experiment.

title: 3  Human intent routing
4  Preservation investigation protocol
text:
4.1 Evidence boundary
This book is the operating record for approved FreeMPE preservation research. It does not authorize or run device experiments automatically. Each numbered page proposes one bounded experiment, states what to preserve, and gives an explicit evaluation rule.
Work through the pages in order with one device at a time. The first run uses the stable identifier seaboard-block-01; replace it only after the device register records the exact model privately.
Before opening Stage 1, create a human-intent specification with $speckit-specify. Select the preservation investigation route and set its execution status to ready to run only after its safety invariants, observation artifacts, and stop conditions are complete. Keep the specification with its other Spec Kit artifacts under ../specs/.
An observation is not a conclusion. Record the device, firmware, host, method, and result before updating any compatibility claim.

title: 4  Preservation investigation protocol
text:
../evidence/records/ contains reviewable observations and conclusions.
../evidence/private/ is for serial numbers, Bluetooth addresses, and other personal identifiers. It is deliberately not version-controlled.
../evidence/captures/ is local staging for raw traffic captures. Review a capture’s contents and redistribution status before moving a selected, shareable derivative into the repository.

title: 4  Preservation investigation protocol
text:
4.2 Sequence

Register the test host and device.
Establish an offline connection.
Characterize standard MIDI and MPE behaviour.
Test an independent sound source.
Test persistence across a power cycle.
Observe the official configuration tool offline.
Capture one configuration change, only after the safe baseline exists.
Write a dependency map and choose the next investigation.

title: 5  Register the test host and device
text:
5.1 Investigation
Which physical device and macOS host are being observed, before any setting, firmware, or software state is changed?
crumbs: 5  Register the test host and device

title: 5  Register the test host and device
text:
Use one Seaboard Block and the M4 MacBook Pro. Do not open ROLI Dashboard, run an updater, change a device setting, or flash firmware. Keep the device disconnected while you create the record. Confirm that an intention specification under ../specs/ selects the preservation-investigation route and is marked ready to run.


From the repository root, copy the two templates:
cp evidence/templates/device-identity.private.yml evidence/private/seaboard-block-01.yml
cp evidence/templates/device-baseline.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-baseline.yml
Put serial number and Bluetooth address only in the private record. In the reviewable baseline, record the date, macOS version, Mac model, device label, connection planned for the test, and the fact that no device state has been changed.


If a version label is visible on the device, packaging, or a previously saved legitimate record, transcribe it as reported, with its source. Do not launch vendor software solely to discover a version at this stage. Leave unknown fields as unknown; unknown is useful evidence.


This stage passes when both records exist, the private record remains outside Git, and the reviewable baseline identifies one device and one host without claiming any MIDI or MPE result. It is acceptable—and expected—for firmware and other fields to remain unknown.
If any setting was changed or an updater was opened, mark the baseline as contaminated, explain why, and begin again with the next untouched device.
crumbs: 5  Register the test host and device

title: 6  Establish an offline connection
text:
6.1 Investigation
Can macOS recognize the controller while the host has no network connection and no ROLI application is running?

title: 6  Establish an offline connection
text:
Confirm ../evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-baseline.yml exists and says that no device configuration has been changed. Close ROLI Dashboard and any other vendor software before connecting the device. Keep the approved preservation-investigation specification active; if its scope changes, pause and revise the specification before proceeding.


Disconnect the Mac from Wi-Fi and Ethernet. Record the time and method in a new file:
cp evidence/templates/offline-connection.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-offline-connection.yml
Then connect the Seaboard Block by USB. In Audio MIDI Setup, inspect the MIDI Studio view and record the displayed device name, whether it appears, and any visible ports. Do not alter device configuration.


If useful, save a redacted screenshot of the MIDI Studio view beside the record. Do not include unrelated devices, account information, or serial numbers. If no device appears, record that absence and the cable/port used; absence is a result, not a reason to try a firmware update.


Mark the record confirmed only if the controller appeared in macOS while the network was disconnected and no vendor tool was running. Otherwise mark it not-confirmed and record the exact visible symptom. This stage answers only operating-system recognition; it does not yet establish MIDI output.

title: 7  Characterize standard MIDI and MPE
text:
7.1 Investigation
What standard MIDI messages does the offline-connected Seaboard emit, and is its expressive behaviour consistent with MPE?
crumbs: 7  Characterize standard MIDI and MPE

title: 7  Characterize standard MIDI and MPE
text:
Confirm that the Stage 2 record is confirmed. Keep the Mac offline, use the same USB connection, and do not open Dashboard or change a setting. This page may run only while the active intention specification still covers passive MIDI observation.


Choose a MIDI event monitor that only listens to the Seaboard input. Record its name and version in a new observation record:
cp evidence/templates/midi-mpe-observation.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-midi-mpe.yml
Do not send MIDI or SysEx messages to the device in this stage.


For each gesture, record message families, channels, and whether you observed the expected change: one note; two simultaneous notes; pressure on one held note; lateral movement of one held note; and vertical movement of one held note. Preserve a short redacted event log only if it contains no unrelated MIDI traffic.


Confirm ordinary MIDI only when note-on and note-off events were observed. Confirm MPE only when the record contains evidence of independently expressive per-note behaviour and the observer/method is named. Otherwise retain unknown—a melodic response alone is not sufficient evidence for MPE.
crumbs: 7  Characterize standard MIDI and MPE

title: 8  Test an independent sound source
text:
8.1 Investigation
Can the controller’s observed MIDI/MPE output drive a non-ROLI sound source while the host remains offline?
crumbs: 8  Test an independent sound source

title: 8  Test an independent sound source
text:
Confirm that seaboard-block-01-midi-mpe.yml records at least ordinary MIDI. Choose a locally installed, non-ROLI instrument or synth and record its name and version. Do not download or purchase software for this experiment. If the intention specification does not name independent playback, revise it before continuing.


Copy the template:
cp evidence/templates/independent-sound.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-independent-sound.yml
Record the MIDI input, sound source, output device, and whether it is configured for ordinary MIDI or MPE. Keep the route as simple as possible: controller to one sound source to one audio output.


Repeat the Stage 3 gesture set and listen for note triggering and expressive response. Record audible results separately from message observations. A synth that cannot interpret MPE does not disprove MPE output; it only limits this particular playback test.


Mark ordinary independent playback confirmed only if notes sounded through a named non-ROLI source offline. Mark expressive independent playback confirmed only if the sound source was configured for MPE and responded as recorded. Keep all other claims separate.
crumbs: 8  Test an independent sound source

title: 9  Test power-cycle persistence
text:
9.1 Investigation
Does the observed baseline behaviour persist after a normal disconnect and reconnection, without a vendor tool or network connection?

title: 9  Test power-cycle persistence
text:
Confirm the previous MIDI/MPE and independent-sound records exist. Do not change configuration before this test; this stage observes persistence of the current state, rather than testing a newly chosen setting. Confirm that a normal power-cycle is within the active specification’s approved scope.


Copy the template:
cp evidence/templates/power-cycle.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-power-cycle.yml
Record the MIDI device name, port appearance, and fixed gesture results before the power cycle. Disconnect normally, wait long enough for the device to power down, reconnect by the same USB path, and repeat exactly the same observations.


Compare the two observations. Record changes in recognition, channel behaviour, pitch response, pressure, or surface response. Do not infer a cause; label each difference as observed, not observed, or unknown.


Confirm baseline persistence only when the same documented observations recur after reconnection. If they differ, report exactly what changed and preserve the record for a later, focused investigation. Do not use Dashboard to repair the state before documenting the failure.

title: 10  Observe Dashboard offline
text:
10.1 Investigation
What can the legitimate, already-installed official configuration application do while offline, and what does it add beyond the preserved controller baseline?

title: 10  Observe Dashboard offline
text:
Confirm that the power-cycle record exists and that the Mac remains offline. Use only an already installed, legitimately obtained application. Do not sign in, update, install, flash firmware, or apply a device setting in this stage. The active specification must explicitly permit observation of Dashboard.


Copy the template:
cp evidence/templates/dashboard-offline.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-dashboard-offline.yml
Record the application name/version, launch result, authentication prompt (if any), visible device state, and which controls are visible or disabled. Treat a login prompt as an observation; do not attempt to bypass it.


Close the application without selecting a configuration control. Reconfirm the ordinary MIDI behaviour from Stage 3. This establishes whether observation alone changed the baseline.


Record Dashboard as offline-capable only for actions actually observed to work offline. Record it as authentication-dependent only when a prompt prevented a named action. Neither outcome determines whether the controller itself works offline.

title: 11  Capture one configuration change
text:
11.1 Investigation
What communication and persistent state accompany one known, reversible configuration change made by the official tool?

title: 11  Capture one configuration change
text:
Proceed only if the previous records exist, the selected control is understood, and the change is reversible without firmware flashing. Choose one variable—for example pitch-bend range—and one before/after value. If recovery is uncertain, stop at Stage 6. The active specification must name this exact control, both values, the capture method, and the stop condition before any change is made.


Copy the metadata template and create a local raw-capture directory:
cp evidence/templates/setting-capture.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-setting-capture.yml
mkdir -p evidence/captures/seaboard-block-01
Record device, firmware if known, application version, transport, capture tool, the exact control, and before value. Start with passive capture where possible.


Capture traffic before, during, and after one change. Repeat the same change, then reverse it. Check the resulting device behaviour and power-cycle persistence. Keep raw capture local until you have reviewed its contents and redistribution status.


Call a message pattern a hypothesis only when repeated captures align with one control change and its reversal. Record direction, payload candidates, device, firmware, persistence, and confidence. Do not send a suspected message back to the device in this stage.

title: 12  Write the dependency map
text:
12.1 Investigation
Which controller capabilities work independently, which depend on an official application, and which remain unknown?

title: 12  Write the dependency map
text:
Review all completed records from Stages 1–7. Do not fill a missing observation from memory, online discussion, or expectation. A missing record remains unknown. Link the map to the active intention specification so its conclusion can decide whether to stop, revise the investigation, begin learning, or open a new software-development intention.


Copy the template:
cp evidence/templates/dependency-map.yml evidence/records/seaboard-block-01-dependency-map.yml
For each capability—offline recognition, MIDI, MPE, independent sound, configuration, persistence, backup/restore, and recovery—record status, evidence file, and next investigation. Link only records that actually support the claim.


Prioritize an unknown that can be resolved by observation. Examples include a different MIDI observer, a controlled power-cycle repeat, or a second passive capture. Do not escalate to firmware work merely because an advanced capability is unknown.


The stage passes when every claimed capability points to a specific evidence record and every unsupported capability remains unknown. The map must name one next low-risk investigation; it must not declare the device simply “free” or “bricked.”
